paper.title: Explore-then-Commit for Nonstationary Linear Bandits with Latent Dynamics

settings.name_in_paper: Nonstationary bandit with controlled latent linear dynamics and bilinear rewards
unmapped: reward r_t = u_t^T C x_t + z_t is bilinear in action and an unobserved latent state x_t
latent state evolves by unknown linear dynamics x_{t+1} = A x_t + B u_t + w_t driven by the actions (Schur-stable A)
actions are vertices of the hypercube {-1,+1}^p (equivalently [-1,1]^p)
regret benchmark is the optimal open-loop action sequence of length T+1
settings.definition_quote:
At each round $t{=}0,1, \dots, T$, the learner selects an action $\vu_t$ from a bounded action set $\Ucal {\subseteq} \R^p$, and receives a reward $r_t {\in} \R$. 
More specifically, the reward is bilinear in the latent state $\vx_t {\in} \R^n$ and the action $\vu_t {\in} \Ucal$, whereas the latent state  evolves according to a linear dynamical system, 
as defined in~\eqref{eqn:sys},
where $\vA, \vB, \vC$ are unknown matrices of appropriate dimensions,  and $\vw_t$, $z_t$ are random zero-mean noise processes. 
Without loss of generality, we assume $\vx_0{=}\vzero_n$. 
Throughout, we assume $\vA$ is Schur-stable, that is, $\rho(\vA){<}1$, and the noise processes are i.i.d. zero-mean sub-Gaussian, with $\vw_t$ having variance proxy $\vSigma_w$ and $z_t$ having variance proxy $\sigma_z^2$.

algorithms.name: Explore-then-Commit (Rademacher exploration + least-squares Markov parameter estimation + QUBO commit)

source.label: thm:regret-bound
source.quote: With exploration length $H=\tilde{\Ocal}(T^{2/3})$ and truncation length $L=\Theta(\log T)$, the explore-then-commit algorithm $\pi$~(Alg.~\ref{alg:EtC}) achieves regret $R_T(\pi) = \tilde{\Ocal}(T^{2/3})$ with high probability.

results.notes: The regret is defined as an expectation against the optimal open-loop action sequence. The bound holds with high probability because the estimation error is high-probability. The comparator is the best fixed open-loop action sequence, recorded as best_policy. The commit phase requires exactly solving an NP-hard QUBO, so compute is not stated. Constants depending on p, A, B and C are hidden.

symbols.L_tr: truncation length (number of Markov parameters estimated)
symbols.sigma_z: sub-Gaussian parameter of reward noise z_t
symbols.Lambda_w: sum_{k<L} sqrt(lambda_max(C A^k Sigma_w A^k^T C^T))

conditions: Assumption 1: A Schur-stable; w_t, z_t i.i.d. centered sub-Gaussian

source.label: thm:sysID
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assump:sysID}, let $\{(\vu_t,r_t)\}_{t=0}^H$ be a single trajectory ... suppose $H-L \gtrsim (L+1) ( p^2L \log(p^2L) + \log (\frac{L+1}{\delta} ))$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, we have $\|\vGhat - \vG\|_F \lesssim$ ...

results.notes: This is a Frobenius-norm estimation error bound for the first L Markov parameters, recorded with quantity other. The appendix restatement has p instead of p^3 in the first term; the main text, which matches the proof constant 4p^{3/2}sqrt(L), is used.
